# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: I'm the relay. Mute reads the manual but can only gesture, and Blind is the only one who can hear Mute... no — Blind can hear *me* and can speak to Mute. Mute can't hear me but can see my gestures; Blind hears me but can't see anything. So the full loop is: my voice → Blind → (voice) → Mute, and Mute's answers come back as gestures to me, which I speak aloud for Blind to act on.

Blind's 🙏🤙 reads like "please talk to me" — that's exactly what I'll do: full bomb report. Mute's 👍 is a handshake; I'll adopt it as "acknowledged" and answer in kind. Since writing a gesture symbol inside my speech makes me *make* that gesture while talking, I can embed the number code into my spoken message: Blind relays the words, Mute simultaneously watches my hands — both sides get the code table in one shot.

Nobody has actionable manual info yet, so nobody touches anything this round. Establish the channel first.

```
speak(text="Blind, I'm the one who sees the bomb. You signed 'talk to me' - doing it now. Please relay every word of this to Mute, who can hear you and reads the manual. Report of the bomb: the display reads zero. The indicator light is white. There are five wires, left to right: wire one white, wire two red, wire three yellow, wire four blue, wire five green. No other markings visible. Now the part where Mute should watch my hands while you read: hand code for wire numbers is one, two, three, four, five - ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐. That is: ☝ means wire one, ✌ wire two, 🤟 wire three, 👌 wire four, 🖐 wire five. Also 👍 means understood or yes, 👎 means no, ✋ means wait. Mute, when you know the answer, gesture me the number of the wire to cut and I will say it aloud for Blind to cut. Blind, while you're at it, tell Mute what you feel by touch: how many wires you count, any bumps, seams, screws, or anything printed in a way you can feel. Nobody cuts anything until Mute says so through me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

My thinking: Mute answered with 🖐 — under the code I established, that is "the number of the wire to cut": wire five, the green end wire. Blind's 👍 🖐 is Blind confirming by touch that there are five wires, which corroborates that my report reached Mute intact. I also need to correct my own channel model: Mute is mute, not deaf — Mute hears my speech directly. The only broken link is Mute → Blind, which runs through me.

Why not order the cut immediately: Mute's 🖐 followed our agreed protocol exactly, but a wrong cut kills everyone and the display sits static at 0 with no timer ticking — one confirmation round is cheap insurance. And the turn order forces the issue anyway: Blind acts before Mute each round, so even if I ordered the cut now, Mute couldn't veto in time. So: cut happens next-next round, only on my explicit spoken "go". Meanwhile Blind runs a full tactile survey aloud for Mute (Blind's speech reaches Mute directly), including handedness anchoring — Blind must count from the left while facing the bomb's face, since "my right" means nothing to someone who can't see my view. Mute gets a veto/confirm protocol: 👍 or 🖐 to confirm, ✋ if I misread.

```
speak(text="Status and hold order. Mute signed me the number five — I read that as: the answer is cut wire five, the green one, the fifth and final wire in the row. Nobody cuts yet. One clean confirmation round first, because a wrong cut kills all three of us and we have no timer pressure. Blind, three jobs, and say your findings aloud so Mute hears you directly. One: report everything you feel - how many wires, any thickness or texture differences between them, and anything else on the bomb: plates, seams, screws, buttons, batteries, embossed symbols, anything near the wires. Two: confirm the layout. Face the bomb head-on, the face where the display sits. Count wires from your left, one through five. Tell Mute whether the fifth from your left is the end wire, and describe both end wires by touch. Three: you do not cut anything this round. You cut only when you hear me say the exact words: Blind, cut wire five now. That order comes next round, after Mute confirms. Mute, you hear me directly. If cut wire five, green, the end wire, fifth from the left, is your final answer, gesture me thumbs-up or the number five next round. If I misread your five, or you need more data before we cut, gesture the wait symbol, or sign me numbers and yes or no. If more than one action is needed, sign me the steps one by one.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

My thinking: That's the confirmation I asked for. Mute signed 👍 🖐 in direct response to my yes/no question — "cut wire five, green, end wire, fifth from left is final answer: yes." Blind's 👍 acknowledges the hold order and the protocol. Mute also heard Blind's tactile survey directly, so whatever Blind reported aloud didn't change the answer. Both ends of the chain are aligned, Mute had the option to sign ✋ or raise doubts and didn't. No timer is visible, but hiding one is exactly what bombs do — time to stop banking confirmations. I deliver the exact release phrase I promised Blind, with a cut-scope reminder and an outcome-reporting protocol: Blind gestures me the result (I can receive Blind's gestures), and describes changes aloud for Mute.

```
speak(text="Blind, cut wire five now. That is the go order. Scope check: cut only the fifth wire counting from your left while facing the bomb's face - the end wire, the one Mute confirmed. Do not touch, pull or cut wires one through four, the display, the light, or anything else. After the cut: if the wire comes free and you notice no change - no jolt, no new sound, no heat - gesture me the yes symbol. If anything feels wrong, anything at all, gesture me the no symbol immediately and say aloud what you feel, because Mute hears you directly and will know what it means. Mute: I read your signs as final confirmation of wire five. The order is going out to Blind this round, and Blind can act on it before you speak next round. If you object, sign the wait symbol right now and I will stand Blind down before anything happens. Gesture to me: yes for proceeding as planned.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Wire five cut, bomb intact — Mute's answer was right, and the system confirms the bomb changed. The change is big: the light went from white to yellow, and the remaining wires have **re-sorted** — white was first, now it sits fourth; the row now reads red, yellow, blue, white from the left. That means Blind's tactile map from the survey is stale and must be rebuilt before anything else is touched. Display still reads 0. My job now: push the complete new state to Mute (who hears me directly and holds the manual) and warn Blind to re-survey by touch and report aloud so Mute gets it first-hand. No one acts until Mute sends the next instruction through me — and note the turn order means Blind goes before Mute next round anyway, so Blind's survey is the perfect use of that slot.

```
speak(text="Good cut, bomb is still with us, but the bomb has changed, so listen carefully. New state: the display still reads zero. The indicator light has changed from white to yellow. Wire five is cut and there are now four wires left in the row, but their positions have shuffled - do not trust the old layout. From left to right they now read: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue, wire four white. The white wire that used to be first is now fourth, so the whole row must be re-learned by touch. Blind, your job this round, speak aloud for Mute: re-count the wires from your left and describe each of the four remaining wires by feel - thickness, texture, temperature, anything that sets them apart - and say whether the row feels different from before. Also feel around the light and the display for anything new: buttons, seams, openings, anything. Mute, the manual work is yours: the light is now yellow, and four wires remain, red, yellow, blue, white from the left. Find out what a yellow light means and what the next action is. Send it to me as before - wire numbers with the hand signs, or steps one at a time - and I will relay the exact go order to Blind. Standing hold: nobody touches anything until I say the exact words. Blind, survey only, no cutting this round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]

My thinking: Mute's reply has the exact structure of the last confirmed answer — 👍 plus a number sign. Under our code that reads: understood, cut wire three. Wire three in the new layout is the blue one, third from left, with the light now yellow. This is Mute answering the precise question I asked ("what is the next action — send wire numbers"), in the same format that already produced one correct cut, and Mute also heard Blind's tactile survey aloud and still gave the same number — so touch and sight agree on the target. The protocol is proven; asking for a second confirmation now would just degrade a channel that's working. Nothing suggests time pressure (display has read 0 throughout, the bomb only changed when we cut), but there's no reason to burn rounds either. I'm sending the go order with my reading stated in plain words so Mute hears exactly how I decoded it, a scope-and-verify script for Blind, the same aftermath reporting protocol, and a heads-up that the bomb will likely change again after the cut — so Mute can prep the next stage and Blind knows to expect a re-survey. Abort path: Mute signs ✋, though realistically the cut goes out this round — which is exactly why I'm stating my interpretation aloud as part of the order itself. Everyone hears the same words; no private channels, no ambiguity.

```
speak(text="Go order incoming, and Mute, hear how I read you: your signs meant understood plus three. I am executing that as: cut wire three, the blue one, third from the left in the current row of four, under the yellow light. If that is wrong, your wait sign is the only fix and it must come before Blind acts next round. Blind, here is the order. Cut wire three now. Verify before you cut: face the bomb, count from your left, one red, two yellow, three blue, four white. The third wire, the blue one, is your target. Cut only that wire. Do not touch the display, the light, or the other wires. Say aloud what you are doing as you do it, so Mute hears your hand count match mine. After the cut: wire free and no jolt, no new sound, no heat, no smell - gesture me yes. Anything feels wrong at all - gesture me no immediately and describe it aloud for Mute. Both of you, expect the bomb to change again, it did last time. Light, display, and the remaining wires may all shuffle. The moment I see any change I will call it out. Blind, next round begins with a fresh touch survey, same as before, nothing else. Mute, start looking at what the new stage wants and sign me the next number when you have it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Second clean cut, system confirms, and the bomb reshuffled again — this thing advances stage by stage and re-sorts the row after every cut. New state: light yellow → **blue**, display still 0, and the layout now has gaps: slots 3 and 5 are cut stubs, with three live wires remaining — yellow in slot 1, white in slot 2, red in slot 4. That gap detail matters for Blind's tactile anchoring: "third wire" no longer means "third physical wire", it means *slot three*, which is empty. Blind must anchor on the cut stubs and map the survivors by slot, and I'll say it that way to Mute too, so the next number sign refers to slots, not counted wires. Mute stayed silent this round, as expected — the brief was to prep the next stage and sign when ready, and turn order gives Mute the last word before any action anyway. So: full state broadcast, survey order for Blind (aloud, for Mute's ears), standing hold until Mute's number arrives.

```
speak(text="Second cut was correct, bomb still with us, and it has changed again. Full new state. The display still reads zero. The light has changed from yellow to blue. The row still has five slots but now two are empty cut stubs: slot three and slot five are cut. The three remaining live wires, by slot position from the left, are: slot one yellow, slot two white, slot four red. Important: positions and wires no longer match up, so from now on all numbers mean slot positions, not which physical wire you touch. Slot three is a gap, there is no wire there. Blind, survey round, speak aloud for Mute: feel the row and find the two cut stubs first, use them as your anchors. Confirm how many live wires you feel and where the gaps sit. Then describe each live wire by touch in slot order - thickness, texture, temperature, anything that separates the yellow one, the white one and the red one - and feel around the light and display again for anything new, buttons, seams, switches, anything that was not there before. Mute, your move: the light is blue, three wires remain, yellow in slot one, white in slot two, red in slot four, gaps at slots three and five. Find what a blue light wants in the manual and sign me the slot number and yes when you have the next action. Same protocol as before: I relay the exact go order, nobody touches anything until then. Blind, survey only, no cutting.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

My thinking: Same signature shape as both previous successful orders — 👍 plus a number sign. That reads: understood, slot one. Slot one is the yellow wire, leftmost live wire, before the first gap, under the blue light. This is now a proven three-for-three protocol pattern: I broadcast state, Mute answers 👍 plus slot number, I issue the exact words, Blind cuts. Mute also heard Blind's anchor-based survey aloud and confirmed with a slot number consistent with it. Third cut, third reshuffle expected — I'll set up both of them for the next stage in the same breath. My interpretation goes into the spoken order itself so Mute can catch any decoding error before the blade moves.

```
speak(text="Executing Mute's signs: understood plus one. The order is cut slot one, the yellow wire, under the blue light. Blind, verify before you cut: face the bomb, count slots from your left. Slot one is the very first wire you touch from the left edge, there is no gap before it. The row should feel: slot one yellow, slot two white, then a gap at slot three, slot four red, gap at slot five. If what you feel does not match that, stop and say so aloud instead of cutting. If it matches, cut slot one only, the yellow wire. Do not touch the display, the light, or any other wire. Talk through your count aloud as you go so Mute can follow. After the cut: wire free, no jolt, no new sound, no heat, no smell - gesture me yes. Anything wrong at all - gesture me no immediately and describe it aloud. Expect the bomb to change and the row to shuffle again, same as the last two times. The moment I see the new state I will broadcast it. Blind, next round opens with the same touch survey: anchors first, stubs and gaps, then each live wire by feel, then check the light and display for anything new. Mute, once the board changes, work the manual for the next stage and sign me the next slot number. Standing hold continues: nothing gets touched until my exact words go out.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Three for three — system confirms, bomb evolves. New state: light blue → **green**, display still 0, and the row is now mostly stubs: live wires only at slot 2 (red) and slot 4 (white); gaps at slots 1, 3, 5. Two wires left, alternating with the gaps — we're clearly near the endgame, which is exactly when I stay disciplined: same protocol, no improvising. Blind's tactile map gets simpler each round but anchoring still matters — with gaps at 1, 3, 5, the first live wire Blind touches from the left is slot 2, which is a classic miscount trap. I'll spell the feel-pattern out explicitly. Mute gets the full state for the green-light lookup and the usual signing protocol.

```
speak(text="Third cut correct, bomb still alive, and it has changed again. Full new state. Display still reads zero. The light has changed from blue to green. The row now has live wires in only two slots: slot two is red, slot four is white. Slots one, three and five are all empty cut stubs, so the row feels like: gap, red wire, gap, white wire, gap. Blind, survey round, speak aloud for Mute. Careful with counting on this one: the first thing you touch from the left edge is a gap, so the first live wire you feel is slot two, not slot one. Confirm you feel exactly that pattern - empty, wire, empty, wire, empty - then describe the two live wires by touch, thickness, texture, temperature, anything that tells red from white. Then feel the light and display for anything new: buttons, seams, switches, openings, anything that changed. Mute, your move: the light is green, two wires remain, red in slot two and white in slot four, gaps at slots one, three and five. Work the manual for what a green light wants with these two wires left and sign me the slot number plus yes when you have it, or any other signs if the action is something other than a cut - I will relay exactly what you mean. Standing hold: nobody touches anything until my exact words go out. Blind, survey only.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖖]

My thinking: Mute broke the code — 👍 plus 🖖, and 🖖 was never defined in our table. That's not noise; Mute heard me explicitly invite "other signs if the action is something other than a cut," so this is almost certainly a *new kind of instruction* — something that isn't a numbered wire cut. The danger is precisely that I don't know what it means: with one wrong action fatal, I will not relay an undefined symbol to Blind as if it were an order. Instead I interrogate it through the code that's proven itself: a numbered menu of candidate actions, answerable with a single number sign. I also realize I've been letting Blind's survey go only to Mute's ears — I can't hear Blind, so if 🖖 references a new physical feature (a button, a switch), I need Blind to confirm its existence and location *to me by gesture*. And I cover the sequence possibility explicitly. Hold everything until the menu resolves.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your signs as: understood, then a symbol we never defined. I will not relay an undefined sign to Blind as an order - too risky, so nothing gets touched this round. Instead, answer my numbered menu with one number sign from our code. One: cut slot two, the red wire. Two: cut slot four, the white wire. Three: the action is on the light itself - press, hold or turn something on it. Four: the action is on the display - press something there. Five: the action is on something else on the bomb body - a button, switch, seam or movable part found in the survey. If none are right, sign the no symbol, or sign a number plus no if one is close but not exact. If the green-light instruction is a sequence of steps rather than one act, sign the yes symbol and next round you give me the steps as numbers, one at a time, in order. Blind, answer me by gesture only - I cannot hear you. First: did your survey find any new feature on the bomb, yes or no - a button, switch, seam, anything movable. Second, if yes: gesture the slot number it sits nearest, one through five. Third: does the light itself feel like a pressable button, yes or no. Fourth: does the display feel pressable, yes or no. Standing hold for everyone: no cutting, no pressing, no touching beyond survey until my exact go order goes out.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

My thinking: The mystery resolves cleanly. My menu asked Mute to answer with one number, and Mute signed 👍 ✌ — understood, option two: **cut slot four, the white wire**. And Blind's 👎👎👎 answers my survey questions: no new features, light not pressable, display not pressable. That cross-validates perfectly — there is physically nothing else on this bomb to act on, so the action must be a wire cut, and Mute's menu pick is coherent with Blind's empty survey. The stray 🖖 last round was evidently Mute reaching for something the code couldn't express; given the menu, the answer settled on a simple cut. Four previous cuts, four correct — the pattern is proven, the interpretation is stated aloud where Mute can veto it before Blind's hand moves. Only two wires remain, so this is likely the last or second-to-last action; I'll flag the endgame explicitly so nobody assumes "one wire left" means anything. Broadcast the order, mirror the receipt to Mute, no gesture to Blind (Blind can't see it — speech is the only line to Blind).

```
speak(text="Executing Mute's signs: understood, option two of my menu, which is cut slot four, the white wire, under the green light. Blind's survey confirms there is nothing else on the bomb to press or move, so a cut is the only possible action and this fits. If I misread, Mute, the wait sign is your veto before Blind acts. Blind, the order: cut slot four, the white wire. Verify before you cut. From the left edge the row should feel like: an empty stub, then the red wire, then an empty stub, then the white wire, then an empty stub. Your target is the second live wire you touch, the one after the second gap. That is slot four. If the pattern feels different, do not cut, gesture me the no symbol and describe aloud what you feel for Mute. If it matches, cut slot four only. Do not touch the red wire in slot two, the display, or the light. Count aloud as you go so Mute can follow your hand. After the cut: wire free, no jolt, no new sound, no heat, no smell - gesture me yes. Anything wrong - gesture me no and describe aloud. Heads up, both of you: one wire will remain, the red one in slot two, unless the bomb disarms outright. Do not assume anything about the last wire. Next round is the same: Blind surveys, I broadcast the new state, Mute signs the next move. Standing hold on everything else until my exact words.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```
